text.p: Nantes and Paris Saint-Germain, who meet in the French first division on Saturday, can measure their fortunes this season on the skill and luck of their goalkeepers.
Nantes, who succeeded PSG as champions in 1995, have not lost in 14 league games since teenager Mickael Landreau took over in goal from long-term injury victim Dominique Casagrande.

The Parisians have lost their defensive solidity since France international keeper Bernard Lama, unbeaten in the first seven games of the season, was hurt saving a penalty at Cannes and needed a cartilage operation.

PSG, top of the standings on points since September but now behind Monaco on goal difference, are in trouble for the second time this season after succesive defeats, at home against lowly Nancy in the first division and away to Lyon in the League Cup.
Lyon's equaliser in a 2-1 win was typical of the current poor form of Lama, who let Alain Caveglia's shot bounce off his chest for Franck Gava to score from the rebound.

Lama's understudy Vincent Fernandez conceded PSG's first goals this season. But the Euro 96 keeper, since returning in October, played in their first loss at Rennes and let in five in a 5-3 defeat at Bordeaux in November.
"We're going to have be strong to resist Nantes, the best French team at the moment," said veteran defender Paul Le Guen.
Le Guen's habitual centre-back partner, French international Alain Roche will miss the match at the Stade de La Beaujoire through injury.
So will Brazil's Leonardo, a major influence in midfield, whose absences through international duty or injury have coincided with PSG's dips in form.
Leonardo missed the defeat at Rennes and the 4-2 loss away to Galatasaray in the second round of the European Cup Winners' Cup.

The Brazilian inspired them to a 4-0 home victory in the second leg and a recovery of their best league form. But it has not lasted and PSG have looked fragile at the midway stage of the championship.
Nantes picked up only two points in their opening seven games of the season and did not win until the 10th match.

But France youth international Landreau responded to the club's call by keeping successive clean sheets in his first two first division matches, a 0-0 draw at Bastia including a penalty save and a 7-0 rout of Nice in Nantes' first win.
With solidity guaranteed at the back Nantes, who have the best attack in the division with 41 goals in 21 games, began a steady climb up the table to their current eighth position.
But coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau warned against complacency.
"Let's not forget that last year, (PSG) came here and won (2-1) when they were also at their worst," he said.
Nantes forward Japhet N'Doram, the division's 14-goal joint top scorer, is doubtful for the match with an ankle injury.
